interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins and no invasion of the seminal vesicles, along with an absence of lymphovascular invasion. The surgical pathology indicated a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and pathological T2 stage without extraprostatic extension. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA of 4.8 and the discrepancy between the biopsy (Gleason 3+3, ISUP grade group 1) and the prostatectomy specimen (Gleason 3+4, ISUP grade group 2). Furthermore, the absence of lymph node removal means nodal status is unknown, which widens the uncertainty regarding potential regional disease. The lack of postoperative PSA data prevents a definitive assessment of the subsequent trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and its subsequent trend would significantly revise this prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 84.76 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 55.09–114.42 months; its coverage has not been validated.
